name: stb_zip (CRC32 routine)
workload: CRC32 checksum of a 1GB in-memory buffer
claimed_speedup: CRC32 of 1GB data: 0.2 sec (stb_zip) vs 1.1 sec (miniz 3.0) = 5.5x
tradeoffs: Header-only single-file C library; only supports store/deflate ZIP entries, not a general-purpose zlib replacement.
caveats: First-party single-table README benchmark; miniz is a widely-used lightweight zlib-compatible library but is not the canonical zlib CRC32 baseline itself, and compiler/flags are unstated.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia search "crc32 zlib"

verification.tier_reason: The README's BENCHMARKS table (Core i7-12700K, 32GB RAM) states 'CRC32 of 1GB data | 0.2 sec | 1.1 sec | 5.5x' vs miniz 3.0. The repo has only README.txt, LICENSE and stb_zip.h: no benchmark code, compiler or flags, so these are numbers without methodology.
verification.notes: The README numbers exist but belong to a different checksum. The only fast path computes CRC-32C, which is wrong for ZIP. The IEEE CRC-32 path matches miniz's byte-table algorithm, so the project is not actually faster at the baseline's function. It is also only 8 stars with 4 commits, all on 2025-08-13. Metadata checked: MIT, not a fork, not archived, stale (last commit 2025-08-13).
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence: the 5.5x fast path computes CRC-32C instead of the IEEE CRC-32 that ZIP requires (breaking its own ZIP CRC check); the correct IEEE path is the same byte-table algorithm as miniz's mz_crc32. No benchmark code.

name: Go standard library crypto (crypto/ed25519, crypto/ecdsa)
baseline: OpenSSL (via the go-openssl cgo bindings formerly used by go-libp2p)
workload: Signature generation and verification for Ed25519 and ECDSA (non-RSA) node identity keys in the go-libp2p networking stack
claimed_speedup: "The Go standard library is faster than OpenSSL for all key types that are not RSA" (covers Ed25519 and ECDSA sign/verify); RSA verify roughly on par between the two, RSA sign slower in both and worse in the Go stdlib
stars_or_usage: 139k stars; standard library used by nearly all Go programs, including go-libp2p (IPFS, Ethereum consensus clients, Filecoin)
tradeoffs: Go-specific implementations, not usable from C++; go-libp2p dropped its OpenSSL bindings entirely as a result and now depends solely on the stdlib
caveats: No concrete numbers or benchmark methodology published in the CHANGELOG entry itself; it is a first-party engineering decision writeup citing internal profiling rather than a reproducible public benchmark, hence tier C rather than A/B
found_via: GitHub code search: "faster than OpenSSL" Ed25519 -> libp2p/go-libp2p CHANGELOG.md ("Removal of OpenSSL" section)

verification.tier_reason: The go-libp2p CHANGELOG (v0.25.0, 'Removal of OpenSSL') makes only a qualitative claim, with no numbers. The linked benchmarks in issue #1952 and PR #1686 show Ed25519 at parity, and even those 'OpenSSL' columns ran Go code (see notes), so no non-RSA measurement against OpenSSL exists.
verification.notes: The record's claim cannot be supported. go-libp2p never used OpenSSL for non-RSA keys, so no head-to-head against OpenSSL for Ed25519 or ECDSA exists anywhere in these sources, and the only real OpenSSL comparison (RSA) shows Go stdlib slower. The record also misparaphrased the RSA line: OpenSSL RSA verify is faster, not on par. If kept, it should sit at tier D with the corrected claim above.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid evidence: go-libp2p's openssl build tag only switched RSA to OpenSSL, so the Ed25519 'OpenSSL' columns in its changelog ran Go code; real OpenSSL RSA is 3-7x faster than Go.
